questions.q: With roughly two hours for fifty to sixty questions, what's the rough time budget per question?
options: A little under two minutes per question on average
Exactly ten minutes per question
Thirty seconds per question with no exceptions
There is no useful average, so budgeting isn't worthwhile
questions.explain: The average matters more than any single question — bank extra time on quick questions to spend on longer scenario ones.

questions.q: What should you do if a question genuinely isn't resolving after reading the full stem and eliminating at least one option?
options: Flag it and move on, then return to it later using the exam's review screen
Keep working it until you're certain, no matter how long it takes
Guess immediately without reading the remaining options
Skip the rest of the exam entirely
questions.explain: Flagging and returning avoids losing disproportionate time on one question at the expense of questions you'd otherwise answer correctly.

questions.q: Why should process of elimination be a default habit rather than a last resort?
options: Removing obviously-wrong options (using Lesson 37's trap patterns) improves your odds before you even try to identify the right answer directly
Because the right answer is always the shortest option
Because elimination only works on true/false questions
Because DP-700 never includes wrong answers that look plausible
questions.explain: Eliminating two clearly-wrong options turns a four-way guess into a coin flip, and often surfaces the right answer by removing the noise.

questions.q: What's the recommended habit after the first 15-20 questions of the exam?
options: A quick pace check — if you're behind schedule, speed up on the easy questions rather than panicking on hard ones
Stop and recalculate your entire study plan
Flag every remaining question automatically
Assume you are always exactly on pace with no need to check
questions.explain: An early pace check lets you correct course by moving faster on quick questions, rather than discovering you're behind near the end.

questions.q: What should you do if the real exam interface warns that a case-study or scenario section can't be revisited once you leave it?
options: Budget extra time specifically for that section, since there's no second pass available
Ignore the warning since it doesn't apply to any Microsoft exam
Rush through it faster than other sections, since it doesn't matter
Skip it entirely and come back at the very end
questions.explain: Some Microsoft exam formats lock a section once you leave it — budgeting extra time there in advance avoids a rushed, unrecoverable pass.
